payload.stem: Recount a real-world engineering challenge where you spearheaded Cross-Functional Influence at foundational responsibility. Use the STAR method.
payload.situation_hint: Detail the Situation, your specific Task, the proactive Action you took, and the quantifiable Result.

criteria.name: STAR Articulation
criteria.description: Clear progression through Situation, Task, Action, and Result.

criteria.name: Leadership Maturity
criteria.description: Highlights personal engineering ownership and measurable business metrics.

model_answer: Situation: Our system experienced sudden traffic spikes that increased error rates by 25%. Task: I was responsible for diagnosing the root cause. Action: I isolated the degraded microservice, applied a circuit breaker, and optimized database indexing. Result: System error rate dropped below 0.01% with 100% SLA adherence.
explanation: High-scoring STAR responses focus on personal ownership, concrete engineering actions, and measurable outcomes.

payload.stem: How do you resolve interpersonal disagreements and maintain psychological safety while driving Cross-Functional Influence?

criteria.name: Conflict Resolution
criteria.description: Uses data and objective metrics rather than authority.

criteria.name: Team Trust
criteria.description: Maintains psychological safety and mutual respect.

model_answer: I de-escalate conflicts by focusing discussions on shared user outcomes, evaluating competing proposals via objective benchmarks, and committing fully to team decisions.
explanation: Constructive resolution relies on framing differences around measurable data and fostering a blameless engineering culture.
